content: As of 12:01 am EDT on May 12, 2023, noncitizen, nonimmigrant air passengers are no longer required to provide proof of full vaccination with an approved COVID-19 vaccine to board a flight to the United States. COVID-19, or Coronavirus Disease 2019, is a respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This virus primarily spreads from person to person through respiratory droplets and small particles that are released when an infected individual coughs, sneezes, or talks. The virus is particularly transmissible in crowded or poorly ventilated indoor environments. Symptoms of COVID-19 can range from none or mild to severe illness. Symptoms typically appear 2 to 14 days after exposure to the virus and may include fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, fatigue, muscle aches, headache, new loss of taste or smell, sore throat, runny nose, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Anyone can contract COVID-19. However, certain individuals are at a higher risk of developing severe illness if they become infected. Vaccination, prior infection, and timely access to testing and treatment can significantly reduce the risk of severe illness from COVID-19. If you have recently had COVID-19, it is important to take additional precautions, such as testing and wearing a mask around others. If you are advised to wear a mask but are unable to do so, you should avoid traveling on public transportation, including airplanes, buses, and trains, where you may be in close proximity to others. Travelers can take several measures to prevent COVID-19. Consider wearing a mask in crowded or poorly ventilated indoor areas, such as public transportation and transportation hubs, especially if you have recently been exposed to someone with COVID-19. Avoid traveling if you are feeling unwell. Consult a healthcare professional before deciding to travel if you are uncertain about your health status. Even if you are up to date with your COVID-19 vaccinations, it is advisable to take multiple preventive steps to add layers of protection against the virus. These steps include staying home if you develop symptoms or suspect you have COVID-19, seeking treatment if you test positive, and getting tested if you develop symptoms before, during, or after travel. Testing is also recommended if you plan to visit someone at higher risk of severe illness from COVID-19 or if you have been in a crowded indoor space, such as an airport terminal, without wearing a mask. If you have traveled and feel unwell, particularly if you develop a fever, consult a healthcare professional. Be sure to inform them about your recent travel history.
